Rashi on Chullin 13a:10:1.english: This is the way he was asking - [Referring to] that which we learned in a mishna (Keilim 17:15), with regard to the hollowing out of an oak or a pomegranate [trunk to make it into a measuring vessel], that they have the status of a [deliberate] act.

Rashi on Chullin 13a:10:2.hebrew: דאורייתא היא - וסמכינן עלה גבי שחיטת עולה, ומכשרינן:
Rashi on Chullin 13a:10:2.english: It is [a law] from the Torah - And we rely upon it regarding the slaughtering of a burnt-offering, and we validate it.

Rashi on Chullin 13a:10:3.hebrew: או דלמא דרבנן הוא - וחומרא הוא דאחמור רבנן לשוויה כלי ליטמא, אבל גבי עולה דקולא הוא, לא:
Rashi on Chullin 13a:10:3.english: Or perhaps it is [only] rabbinic - It is a stringency that the Rabbis imposed, to render it [the thought] a vessel that can become impure; but with regard to a burnt-offering, where it [would be] a leniency, it is not [so].

Rashi on Chullin 13a:10:4.hebrew: מדרבנן יש לו - ולחומרא, גבי היפך בהם דהכשירן:
Rashi on Chullin 13a:10:4.english: By rabbinic law he has [effective thought] - And this is a stringency, regarding [the case of] turning them over, which renders them fit [susceptible to impurity].

Rashi on Chullin 13a:10:5.english: By Torah law, he does not have [effective thought] - And regarding the first dilemma, concerning the burnt offering [the case above, where the minor moved the animal from the south to the north and slaughtered it there], we do not rely on this [resolution].

Rashi on Chullin 13a:11:1.hebrew: מנין למתעסק בקדשים שהוא פסול - כלומר מנין למתעסק שפסול בקדשים, כגון מתעסק בסכין להגביהו או לזורקו ושחט בקדשים שלא נתכוין לשום שחיטה, אבל נתכוין לשום שחיטה בעלמא כשר, אלא שלא עלה לבעלים לשם חובה:
Rashi on Chullin 13a:11:1.english: From where [do we derive] that one who acts unintentionally (mit'assek) with consecrated animals is disqualified - That is to say, from where do we derive that one who acts unintentionally is disqualified with regard to consecrated animals - for example, one who was engaged with a knife in order to lift it or throw it, and [in doing so] slaughtered consecrated animals without intending any act of slaughter at all. But if he intended slaughter in a general sense, it is valid, except that it does not count for the owners as fulfilling their obligation.

Rashi on Chullin 13a:11:2.hebrew: זו בידינו היא - מקרא זה הייתי יודע, ומכאן אנו למדים שמצוה להתכוין, ואני שאלתי לעכב מנין, שאם לא נתכוין יהא פסול:
Rashi on Chullin 13a:11:2.english: This we already have - I already knew this verse, and from it we learn that there is a mitzva to intend [properly when performing the rite]. But what I asked was from where [do we know] that it is indispensable - that if one did not intend, it is invalid.

Rashi on Chullin 13a:11:3.english: You shall sacrifice it according to your will - Scripture repeated this [requirement] to make it indispensable [to the sacrifice's validity].

Rashi on Chullin 13a:12:1.hebrew: שחיטת עובד כוכבים - אפילו כהלכתה ואחרים רואין אותו:
Rashi on Chullin 13a:12:1.english: The slaughter of a non-Jew - Even if it was done according to the halachic requirements, and others were watching him [to ensure it was performed correctly].

Rashi on Chullin 13a:12:2.english: And it renders impure through carrying - The Gemara asks: Isn't this obvious?

Rashi on Chullin 13a:13:1.hebrew: הא אמר - לקמן בהשוחט (חולין דף לח:), דאפי' שחטה ישראל לצורך עובד כוכבים אסורה בהנאה, שסתם מחשבת עובד כוכבים לעבודת כוכבים:
Rashi on Chullin 13a:13:1.english: This is what he said - Later, in [the chapter] HaShochet (Chullin 38b), [it teaches] that even if a Jew slaughtered [an animal] for the sake of a non-Jew, it is forbidden for benefit, since an unspecified intent of a non-Jew is [presumed to be] for idol worship.

Rashi on Chullin 13a:14:1.hebrew: ר' אמי מתני הכי שחיטת עובד כוכבים נבלה הא דמין לעבודת כוכבים - במין ישראל קא מיירי. והך דוקיא דמתניתין הכי דייק מינה, ולסיועי לתנא דברייתא. ורבי אמי לא פליג אדרבי חייא, דודאי מתניתין דלא כרבי אליעזר, אלא לא אצטריך ליה למידק, דממילא שמעינן לה, דמדקרי ליה נבלה ש"מ מותרת בהנאה:
Rashi on Chullin 13a:14:1.english: Rabbi Ami taught it this way: The slaughter of a gentile [renders the animal] a carcass, but [that of] a heretic is for idol worship - He is speaking of a Jewish heretic. And it is from this precise wording of the mishna that he deduces this, and [he does so] in order to lend support to the tanna who taught the baraita. And Rabbi Ami does not disagree with Rabbi Chiyya that the mishna is certainly not in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer; rather, [he holds that] it was not necessary to derive it from such a precise inference, since we can learn it on its own - for from the fact that it calls it a "carcass," we may conclude that it is permitted for benefit.

Rashi on Chullin 13a:14:2.hebrew: תנינא להא דת"ר - וש"מ דהלכתא כברייתא, מדמסייע ליה דוקיא דמתניתין:
Rashi on Chullin 13a:14:2.english: We learn this which the Rabbis taught - And from this deduce that the halacha follows the baraita, since the precise inference of the mishna supports it.

Rashi on Chullin 13a:14:3.hebrew: שחיטת מין - דישראל, וכ"ש דעובד כוכבים, והא מתניתין מיהא בישראל קיימא, מדקאמר פירותיו טבלים ובניו ממזרים. בסדר זרעים שנינו, אומר היה רבי אליעזר: פת כותי כבשר חזיר, במסכת שביעית (פ"ח מ"י):
Rashi on Chullin 13a:14:3.english: The slaughter of a heretic [min] - Of a Jewish [heretic], and all the more so of a non-Jew. And this mishna, in any case, is referring to a Jew, since it says: "his fruits are tevel [untithed] and his sons are mamzerim." We learned in Seder Zeraim, Rabbi Eliezer used to say [that] the bread of a Samaritan is like the meat of a pig, in Tractate Sheviit (chapter 8, mishna 10).

Rashi on Chullin 13a:14:4.english: His books - [Meaning] the Torah, Prophets, and Writings, which a heretic wrote.

Rashi on Chullin 13a:14:5.hebrew: כספרי קוסמין - נביאי הבעל דלשם עבודת כוכבים כתבו, והכי נמי אמרינן במסכת גיטין (דף מה:), ספר תורה שכתבו מין ישרף:
Rashi on Chullin 13a:14:5.english: Like the books of sorcerers - [Referring to] the prophets of Baal, who wrote [their books] for the sake of idol worship. And similarly we say in Tractate Gittin (page 45b): A Torah scroll that a sectarian wrote is to be burned.

Rashi on Chullin 13a:1:1.hebrew: ואין להן מחשבה - כגון מצא לקליפת אגוז כמו שהיה, וחשיב עליה למוד, או אפילו מדד בה, אלא שלא עשה בה מעשה לשם כלי, ואם בן דעת חשב עליהן טמאין במחשבה, דתנן (כלים פכ"ה מ"ט) כל הכלים יורדין לידי טומאתן במחשבה:
Rashi on Chullin 13a:1:1.english: They have no [effective] intent - For example, one found a nutshell just as it was [in its natural, unworked state] and had in mind to use it for measuring, or even actually measured with it, but did not perform any action on it to make it into a vessel. Now, if a person of sound mind had had this intent about it, it would become susceptible to impurity through intent alone, as it was taught (Keilim 25:9): "All vessels become susceptible to their impurity through intent."

Rashi on Chullin 13a:2:1.english: Mere thought alone is not what he is asking about - For this he has already heard [i.e., it is obvious to him that mere intention, without an accompanying act, has no effect].

Rashi on Chullin 13a:2:2.hebrew: מחשבתו ניכרת מתוך מעשיו - לפי ראות עינינו, אבל אין אנו יודעין אם עשה מעשה זה לשם מחשבה זו:
Rashi on Chullin 13a:2:2.english: His intent is discernible from his actions - According to what our eyes perceive, but we do not [actually] know whether he did this act for the sake of this intent.

Rashi on Chullin 13a:3:1.hebrew: ואתיוה לצפון - ולא אמר על שם כך אני מוליכה לשם, לפי שאינה כשרה בדרום:
Rashi on Chullin 13a:3:1.english: And they brought it to the north - He did not say, "It is for this reason that I am bringing it there," i.e., because it is not valid [to slaughter it] in the south.

Rashi on Chullin 13a:3:2.english: Or perhaps it is a matter of location, which did not happen to work out for him - The first location did not seem suitable to him.

Rashi on Chullin 13a:4:1.hebrew: מפני הכנימה - כוצונ"ש שבפולים ועדשים, כמו ותהי הכנם (שמות ח):
Rashi on Chullin 13a:4:1.english: Because of the lice - [In Old French:] "cusençon" - like [the weevils] that infest beans and lentils, similar to "and there came lice" (Exodus 8).

Rashi on Chullin 13a:4:2.hebrew: אינן בכי יותן - דלא ניחא ליה בהאי טל, ולא הוה הכשר להורידן לידי טומאתן אם יגע בהם שרץ לאחר זמן, דבעינן "כי יותן" דומיא ד"כי יתן" דניחא ליה:
Rashi on Chullin 13a:4:2.english: They are not [included under] "when it is put" - Because he is not pleased with this dew, it would not serve as an enabler to bring them to their susceptibility to impurity if a creeping creature touched them afterward. For we require that "when it is put" be similar to "when he puts" - which implies that he is pleased with it.

Rashi on Chullin 13a:4:3.hebrew: ואם נתכוין לכך - בין בשעת העלאה ובין לאחר מכאן, קודם שינגב הטל מעליהם:
Rashi on Chullin 13a:4:3.english: And if he intended for this - Whether at the time of taking [the produce] up to the roof, or afterward - as long as it is before the dew dries off of them.

Rashi on Chullin 13a:4:4.hebrew: הרי הן בכי יותן - דהכי אמרינן בדוכתא אחריתי, עודהו הטל עליהן ושמח, הרי הן בכי יותן, ואע"פ שלא נתכוין קודם לכן אלא כשראה שמח:
Rashi on Chullin 13a:4:4.english: They are [rendered susceptible to impurity] as if water had been put [on them] - For so do we say elsewhere: while the dew is still upon them and one is glad [about it], they are [considered] as if water had been put [on them], even though he did not intend this beforehand, but only became glad when he saw it.

Rashi on Chullin 13a:5:1.english: A deaf-mute, an imbecile, or a minor brought them up - Because of the lice infesting it.

Rashi on Chullin 13a:5:2.english: Even though he intended it - [This means: he intended it] after the dew had [already] fallen upon them.

Rashi on Chullin 13a:5:3.hebrew: אינן בכי יותן - שאין מחשבתם מחשבה, והכשר במחשבה תלוי, והאי מעשה דעלייה לאו מעשה הוא, דמפני הכנימה העלום:
Rashi on Chullin 13a:5:3.english: They are not included in [the verse] "when water is placed" - Since their intent is not [valid] intent, and rendering [produce] susceptible to impurity depends on intent. And this act of bringing [the produce] up [to the roof] is not considered an act, since it was on account of the infestation that they brought it up.

Rashi on Chullin 13a:6:1.english: They only taught [this] - For even if they intended [it], that is not considered [valid] intent.

Rashi on Chullin 13a:6:2.english: Except where he did not turn them over - After the dew had fallen upon them from one side, [he did not turn them] so that it would fall upon them from the other side as well.

Rashi on Chullin 13a:6:3.hebrew: אבל היפך בהן - דמעשיו מוכיחין, אע"פ שלא פירש מחשבתו, הואיל וניכר שדעתו לכך, הרי הן בכי יותן. דאי בשפירש מחשבתו בשעת מעשה, לא איצטריך רבי יוחנן לאשמועינן, דהא בהדיא תנן דיש להן מעשה:
Rashi on Chullin 13a:6:3.english: But he turned them over - [In such a case] his actions prove [his intent], even though he did not articulate his thought, since it is evident that his mind was set on this, so they are indeed included under [the requirement derived from] "which he gave" (כי יתן). For if [Rabbi Yochanan's ruling referred to a case] where he had articulated his thought at the time of the act, Rabbi Yochanan would not have needed to teach it, since we already learned explicitly that they [a deaf-mute, an imbecile, and a minor] have [legally significant] actions.

Rashi on Chullin 13a:7:1.hebrew: הכי קא מיבעיא דאורייתא או דרבנן - הא דאמרינן, ושמעתי מרבותי, דמחשבתו ניכרת מתוך מעשיו הויא מחשבה, כאילו פירשה בשעת מעשה:
Rashi on Chullin 13a:7:1.english: Thus the question is: is it Biblical or Rabbinic - This refers to what we said - and I heard from my teachers - that when one's intent is discernible from his actions, it is [treated as legally valid] intent, as if he had explicitly stated it at the time of the act.

Rashi on Chullin 13a:7:2.english: It is Biblical - And we rely on this even to rule leniently, such as in the dilemma above, in the case of one who brought a burnt-offering from the south to the north, and they deem it valid.

Rashi on Chullin 13a:7:3.hebrew: או דרבנן - היא וחומרא בעלמא הוא דאמור רבנן ניהוי מעשה, וכי היפך בהן ניהוי הכשר, אבל מדאורייתא לא הוי מעשה. וגבי עולה דקולא הוא, לא אמרו כן, שלא אמרו חכמים דבריהם להקל מדברי תורה דנמצאו עוקרין, אלא להחמיר ולעשות סייג:
Rashi on Chullin 13a:7:3.english: Or is it rabbinic - This is merely a stringency that the Rabbis stated: that it should be considered an act, and that if he reversed [his intent] partway through, it should be considered a valid preparation. But by Torah law, it would not be considered an act. And with regard to a burnt-offering, where [treating it as an act] would be a leniency, they did not say so, since the Sages did not state their rulings to be lenient against the words of the Torah - for that would amount to uprooting it - but only to be stringent and erect a fence.

Rashi on Chullin 13a:8:1.hebrew: יש להן מעשה - אם עשו מעשה מוכיח על מחשבתן, ופירשו שעל דעת כן עושים, וכדפרשינן לעיל שהביא עולה לצפון ופירש שמפני שדרום פסול לה הוא מביאה לצפון:
Rashi on Chullin 13a:8:1.english: They have an action - [This means] that they performed an act demonstrating their intent, and they stated explicitly that they were acting with that intent - as we explained above, [in the case] where he brought a burnt-offering to the north and stated explicitly that he was bringing it to the north because the south was unfit for it.

Rashi on Chullin 13a:9:1.hebrew: ותיבעי ליה מחשבה - שחיטה גרידתא ופירש לשם עולה, ושחיטה לאו מעשה מוכיח על המחשבה הוא, שכל השחיטות שוות:
Rashi on Chullin 13a:9:1.english: And let him raise the question of [mere] intent - [I.e.,] a case of plain slaughtering, where he stated [verbally] that it was for the sake of a burnt-offering, and the slaughtering itself is not an act that demonstrates the intent, since all acts of slaughter look the same.

Tosafot on Chullin 13a:11:1.hebrew: בעא מיניה שמואל מרב הונא - משמע שהיה שמואל קטן מרב הונא, וכן בריש גיטין (דף ה.) ובפ' יש בערכין (ערכין טז:) הוו יתבי רב הונא וחייא בר רב קמי שמואל, משמע כתלמיד היושב לפני רבו. ובפרק קמא דגיטין (דף יא:) יתיב רב הונא קמי רבי ירמיה, ורבי ירמיה חבירו של רבי זירא הוה, כדמוכח בנדה (דף כג.): בעא מיניה רבי ירמיה מרבי זירא כו', עד כאן הביאו רבי ירמיה לרבי זירא לידי גיחוך ולא גחך. ורבי זירא תלמידו של רב יהודה, דהוה משתמיט מיניה למיסק לארעא דישראל, ורב יהודה תלמידו של רב ושמואל, והיה קורא רבי ירמיה לרב הונא דרדקי (גיטין דף יא:). ויש לומר דתרי רב הונא הוו, ומיהו ההוא דערכין (דף טז:) על כרחך תלמידו של רב הוה, כדמוכח התם:
Tosafot on Chullin 13a:11:1.english: Shmuel inquired of Rav Huna - This implies that Shmuel was junior to Rav Huna. And similarly, at the beginning of Gittin (5a) and in the chapter "Yesh BeArakhin" (Arakhin 16b), Rav Huna and Chiya bar Rav were sitting before Shmuel, which implies [that they were] like a student sitting before his teacher. And in the first chapter of Gittin (11b), Rav Huna sat before Rabbi Yirmeya; and Rabbi Yirmeya was a colleague of Rabbi Zeira, as is proven in Niddah (23a): "Rabbi Yirmeya inquired of Rabbi Zeira, etc." - up to where it says that Rabbi Yirmeya brought Rabbi Zeira to the point of laughter, yet he did not laugh. And Rabbi Zeira was a disciple of Rav Yehuda, for he used to avoid him so that he could go up to the Land of Israel; and Rav Yehuda was a disciple of Rav and Shmuel. And Rabbi Yirmeya used to call Rav Huna "the teacher of children" (Gittin 11b). And one can say that there were two [different sages named] Rav Huna; however, that [Rav Huna] mentioned in Arakhin (16b) must necessarily have been a disciple of Rav, as is proven there.

Tosafot on Chullin 13a:11:2.hebrew: מנין למתעסק בקדשים שהוא פסול - פירש בקונטרס מתעסק בסכין להגביהו ולזרוק אותו, וקשה דבכה"ג אפילו בחולין פסול לרבנן, אפילו מתכוין לחתיכה כגון לנעצה בכותל, כדמוכח בפרק ב' (לקמן חולין לא.), עד שיתכוין לחתיכת סימנין. ונראה דהאי מתעסק בקדשים היינו דמתכוין לחתיכת סימנים ולא לשם זביחה, דבחולין כשר ובקדשים פסול. ועוד יש מתעסק אחר, כגון של קדשים שסבור שהוא חולין ושחטו, דפסול מטעם מתעסק, כדאמרינן בזבחים בסוף פרק ב"ש (זבחים דף מו:) דמשום חולין פסולה; ותרוייהו מושחט את בן הבקר נפקא:
Tosafot on Chullin 13a:11:2.english: From where do we know that mit'asek [acting inadvertently] with kodshim is invalid? - Rashi explained that mit'asek means that he intends [only] to lift the knife and throw it. And this is difficult, for in such a case even with chullin it is invalid according to the Rabbis, even if he intends to cut - such as to stick it into a wall - as is proven in chapter 2 (below, Chullin 31a), unless he intends to cut the simanim (the trachea and gullet). And it seems that this mit'asek with regard to kodshim means that he intends to cut the simanim but not for the sake of slaughtering, for with chullin this is valid, but with kodshim it is invalid. And furthermore, there is another [kind of] mit'asek - such as an animal of kodshim which he thought was chullin, and he slaughtered it - which is invalid on account of [the principle of] mit'asek, as we say in Zevachim, at the end of Perek Beit Shammai (Zevachim 46b), that it is invalid because [he thought it was] chullin; and both of these are derived from "[and he shall] slaughter the bull" [Vayikra 1:5].

Tosafot on Chullin 13a:14:1.hebrew: פיתו פת כותי - בפירקי דרבי אליעזר (פ' לח) יש, דעזרא וזרובבל בן שאלתיאל ויהושע בן יהוצדק נידו אותן בשלש מאות כהנים ובשלש מאות תינוקות ובשלש מאות ספרי תורה, והיו תוקעין והלוים משוררים, ומסיימים בה: מכאן אמרו, כל האוכל פת כותי כאילו אוכל בשר חזיר:
Tosafot on Chullin 13a:14:1.english: His bread is Cuthean bread - In Pirkei D'Rabbi Eliezer (ch. 38) it states that Ezra, Zerubbabel ben Shealtiel, and Yehoshua ben Yehotzadak excommunicated them with three hundred priests, three hundred children, and three hundred Torah scrolls; and they would blow [shofars], and the Levites would sing, and they would conclude with it: from here they said, whoever eats Cuthean bread, it is as if he eats pig meat.
